title: City of Hot Springs receives more than $340,000 Entergy Arkansas energy efficiency incentives in 2026
summary: The City of Hot Springs has received more than $340,000 in incentives this year through Entergy Arkansas’s Entergy Solutions CitySmart program, including $288,467.07 for energy efficiency improvements…
body_markdown:
HOT SPRINGS, Ark. – The City of Hot Springs has received more than $340,000 in incentives this year through Entergy Arkansas’s Entergy Solutions CitySmart program, including $288,467.07 for energy efficiency improvements at the Davidson Wastewater Treatment Plant.


The city is a longtime participant in the CitySmart program, which helps local governments and other organizations identify opportunities to reduce energy consumption, lower operating costs and maximize the value of their investments.


In addition to improvements at the Davidson Wastewater Treatment Plant, the city’s 2026 projects include the conversion of a church on Hobson Avenue into a community resource center, featuring lighting, heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC), and commercial kitchen upgrades. Other projects include construction of Fire Station No. 6 on Lakeshore Drive and the new Amity Water Treatment Plant, as well as renovations to the former Weyerhaeuser laboratory facility at 900 Whittington Avenue, which now houses city offices. The office renovations included lighting, lighting controls, HVAC upgrades and thermostat setback controls.


Ongoing improvements at the Davidson Wastewater Treatment Plant include new blower equipment and upgrades to its ultraviolet (UV) treatment system.


Collectively, these projects have saved the City of Hot Springs 2,071,017 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of electricity. The city has received $340,876.72 in incentives through Entergy Solutions, helping offset project costs while delivering long-term energy savings.


“In today’s environment, it’s important to pursue cost savings wherever possible. Sometimes that means making a larger investment upfront to achieve significant savings over the long term,” said Pat McCabe, mayor of Hot Springs. “We are very pleased and grateful to receive this incentive check from Entergy Solutions for the energy efficiency improvements we have implemented across several projects at the Davidson Wastewater Treatment Plant.”


“One of our responsibilities at City Hall, and certainly my responsibility as mayor, is to be a good steward of our citizens’ resources,” McCabe continued. “By investing in energy-efficient technologies, we are reducing operating costs and creating long-term value for our community. We appreciate the Entergy Solutions team for their partnership, expertise and for helping verify the energy savings we have achieved through these projects.”


“We are incredibly appreciative of the partnership we have with Entergy and the Entergy Solutions program,” said Bill Burrough, city manager for Hot Springs. “We’ve completed a number of projects together over the years, and each time I’m impressed by the impact these investments make. The savings go beyond just dollars and cents. They also reflect our commitment to environmental stewardship and responsible use of resources.”


“This partnership helps us make improvements that benefit both our community and the environment,” Burrough continued. “We’re grateful for the support and expertise that the Entergy Solutions team brings to these projects.”


“Hot Springs is a thriving community, and all of these exciting upgrades throughout the city have been fun to watch come to life,” said Marshunda Jones, customer service manager for Entergy Arkansas. “We are thrilled that we could assist the city in making these projects as efficient as possible.”


Entergy Arkansas’s CitySmart program, an offering of Entergy Solutions, helps organizations identify energy-saving opportunities specific to their facilities, prioritize energy conservation measures and achieve long-term electricity savings.


Organizations can earn financial incentives by completing qualifying energy efficiency projects and improving the efficiency of their operations.
